Viagem avançada: imprevistos, reclamaçõe: Advanced travel: unexpected problems, complaints and the passive voice
Resolver imprevistos em viagem (voo canc: Handle unexpected problems while traveling (cancelled flight, lost luggage, a problem with your room), make a polite complaint and use the passive voice to talk about facts.
PASSO 1: comece calmo e educado: «Excuse: STEP 1: start calm and polite: «Excusez-moi, je voudrais signaler un problème.» STEP 2: describe the fact without accusing: «La climatisation ne marche pas.» «Mes bagages ne sont pas arrivés.» STEP 3: say what you want, using the conditional: «Je voudrais être remboursé.» «Pourriez-vous changer ma chambre ?» STEP 4: ask for a solution: «Que pouvez-vous faire pour moi ?» STEP 5: formal formulas: «Je vous demande de bien vouloir…», «Je souhaiterais obtenir…» STEP 6: if necessary, insist without aggression: «Je comprends, mais ce n'est pas acceptable.»
em português «eu quero meu dinheiro de v: In both English and French, tone and context matter. «Je veux un remboursement» is grammatical but can sound blunt; «Je voudrais être remboursé» or «Pourriez-vous me rembourser ?» is often more tactful when requesting help.
Faça em voz alta uma reclamação educada:: Make a polite complaint aloud: your hotel room is dirty and you want to change it.
Recomende em voz alta um livro ou filme,: Recommend aloud a book or film, saying what you liked and what you did not like.
PASSO 1: voz passiva = «être» + particíp: STEP 1: the passive uses «être» + a past participle that agrees with the subject: «Le vol est annulé.» «Les bagages sont perdus.» STEP 2: the form of «être» locates the event or state in time: «Le vol a été annulé» (passé composé), «Le vol sera annulé» (future), «Le vol était annulé» (imparfait). STEP 3: an agent is often introduced with «par»: «Le vol a été annulé par la compagnie.» STEP 4: some verbs of feeling or state use «de»: «Il est aimé de tous.» STEP 5: in conversation, an active sentence with «on» is often an alternative: «On a annulé le vol.» STEP 6: «se faire» + infinitive can describe something that happens to someone: «Je me suis fait voler mon sac.» Its meaning depends on context; it is not a universal passive.
em português «o voo foi cancelado» é igu: English also uses a passive in “the flight was canceled.” In French, the participle agrees with the subject: «les bagages sont perdus». You can also use active «on»: «on a perdu mes bagages». «Je me suis fait voler mon sac» means “I had my bag stolen”; the French participle «fait» remains unchanged before an infinitive.
Descreva em voz alta uma viagem em que t: Describe aloud a trip where everything went wrong, using at least four sentences in the passive voice or with «on».
Diga duas frases pedindo algo a um hotel: Say two sentences asking a hotel for something with «pourriez-vous».
PASSO 1: peça informação: «Pouvez-vous m: STEP 1: ask for information: «Pouvez-vous me dire pourquoi mon vol a été retardé ?» STEP 2: ask for alternatives: «Y a-t-il un autre vol aujourd'hui ?» STEP 3: give the details: «Mon numéro de vol est AF 123.» STEP 4: declare the loss: «Je voudrais faire une déclaration de perte.» STEP 5: keep the record: «Pouvez-vous me donner un justificatif ?»
em português «poderia me dizer…?» é cort: In English, “could you tell me…?” is polite; in French, «pouvez-vous me dire» and «pourriez-vous me dire» both work. A «justificatif» is supporting documentation; depending on the situation, it may be a receipt, confirmation or other proof.
Marie fala com a atendente da companhia: Marie talks to the airline agent.
— Bom dia, meu voo para Lyon foi cancela: — Good morning, my flight to Lyon was cancelled. What can I do?
— Sinto muito. Há outro voo às dezoito h: — I'm very sorry. There is another flight at six p.m.
— Muito bem. Mas minha bagagem foi despa: — Fine. But my luggage was checked onto the first flight.
— Não se preocupe, ela será transferida: — Don't worry, it will be transferred automatically.
— Poderia me dar um comprovante para o r: — Could you give me a receipt for the taxi refund?
